title: चतुरशीत्यधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Janamejaya asks about the great fear Lomasha had spoken of. Vaishampayana tells how the Sun appeared to Karna in a dream, warning that Indra would come disguised as a Brahmin to beg his natural armour and earrings, which make him invincible; Karna replies that he cannot refuse a Brahmin, even at the cost of his life.
summary.kn: ಲೋಮಶರು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದ ಮಹಾಭಯದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಜನಮೇಜಯನು ಕೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ತನ್ನನ್ನು ಅಜೇಯನನ್ನಾಗಿಸುವ ಸಹಜ ಕವಚ ಕುಂಡಲಗಳನ್ನು ಬೇಡಲು ಇಂದ್ರನು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣವೇಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರುವನೆಂದು ಸೂರ್ಯನು ಕನಸಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಕರ್ಣನನ್ನು ಎಚ್ಚರಿಸಿದನು; ಪ್ರಾಣ ಹೋದರೂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣನನ್ನು ನಿರಾಕರಿಸಲಾರೆ ಎಂದು ಕರ್ಣನು ಉತ್ತರಿಸಿದನು ಎಂದು ವೈಶಂಪಾಯನರು ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: जनमेजय लोमश द्वारा बताए गए महाभय के बारे में पूछते हैं। वैशम्पायन बताते हैं कि सूर्य ने स्वप्न में कर्ण को चेतावनी दी कि इन्द्र ब्राह्मण वेश में आकर उसके सहज कवच-कुण्डल माँगेंगे, जो उसे अजेय बनाते हैं; कर्ण उत्तर देता है कि प्राण जाने पर भी वह ब्राह्मण को मना नहीं कर सकता।
summary.te: లోమశుడు చెప్పిన మహాభయం గురించి జనమేజయుడు అడుగుతాడు. తనను అజేయునిగా చేసే సహజ కవచకుండలాలను అడగడానికి ఇంద్రుడు బ్రాహ్మణవేషంలో వస్తాడని సూర్యుడు కలలో కర్ణుని హెచ్చరించాడని, ప్రాణం పోయినా బ్రాహ్మణుని నిరాకరించలేనని కర్ణుడు బదులిచ్చాడని వైశంపాయనుడు చెబుతాడు.
summary.ta: லோமஶர் சொன்ன பெரும் அச்சம் பற்றி ஜனமேஜயன் கேட்கிறான். தன்னை வெல்ல முடியாதவனாக்கும் இயற்கைக் கவச குண்டலங்களை இரக்க இந்திரன் அந்தண வேடத்தில் வருவான் என்று சூரியன் கனவில் கர்ணனை எச்சரித்ததையும், உயிர் போனாலும் அந்தணனை மறுக்க முடியாது என்று கர்ணன் பதில் சொன்னதையும் வைஶம்பாயனர் சொல்கிறார்.
summary.ml: ജനമേജയൻ, ലോമശൻ പറഞ്ഞ ആ വലിയ ഭയത്തെക്കുറിച്ച് ചോദിക്കുന്നു. വൈശമ്പായനൻ പറയുന്നു: ഒരു സ്വപ്നത്തിൽ സൂര്യൻ കർണ്ണന് പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെട്ട് മുന്നറിയിപ്പ് നൽകുന്നു: അദ്ദേഹത്തെ അജയ്യനാക്കുന്ന സ്വാഭാവിക കവചവും കുണ്ഡലങ്ങളും യാചിക്കാൻ ഇന്ദ്രൻ ബ്രാഹ്മണവേഷത്തിൽ വരും. ബ്രാഹ്മണനെ നിരസിക്കാനാവില്ലെന്നും, അതിന് ജീവൻ വിലയായാലും, കർണ്ണൻ മറുപടി നൽകുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 3.284; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Apr 11 2022

verses.text: जनमेजय उवाच

meaning.en: Janamejaya said:

verses.text:
यत्तत्तदा महाब्रह्मँल्लोमशो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
इन्द्रस्य वचनादेत्य पाण्डुपुत्रं युधिष्ठिरम् ॥

meaning.en: Great brahmin, what did Lomasha say that time, when he came on Indra's word to Yudhishthira, son of Pandu?

verses.text:
यच्चापि ते भयं तीव्रं न च कीर्तयसे क्वचित् ।
तच्चाप्यपहरिष्यामि सव्यसाचाविहागते ॥

meaning.en: And the intense fear you never mention anywhere, of which he said, I will remove it when Arjuna comes here?

verses.text:
किं नु तद्विदुषां श्रेष्ठ कर्णं प्रति महद्भयम् ।
आसीन्न च स धर्मात्मा कथयामास कस्यचित् ॥

meaning.en: Best of the knowing, what was that great fear regarding Karna? And why did the righteous Yudhishthira tell no one?

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
अहं ते राजशार्दूल कथयामि कथामिमाम् ।
पृच्छते भरतश्रेष्ठ शुश्रूषस्व गिरं मम ॥

meaning.en: I will tell you this story, tiger among kings, since you ask, best of Bharatas; listen to my words.

verses.text:
द्वादशे समतिक्रान्ते वर्षे प्राप्ते त्रयोदशे ।
पाण्डूनां हितकृच्छक्रः कर्णं भिक्षितुमुद्यतः ॥

meaning.en: When the twelfth year had passed and the thirteenth arrived, Indra, who works for the good of the Pandavas, prepared to beg from Karna.

verses.text:
अभिप्रायमथो ज्ञात्वा महेन्द्रस्य विभावसुः ।
कुण्डलार्थे महाराज सूर्यः कर्णमुपागमत् ॥

meaning.en: Knowing Indra's intention, Surya, the maker of light, came to Karna, great king, concerning the earrings.

verses.text:
महार्हे शयने वीरं स्पर्ध्यास्तरणसंवृते ।
शयानमभिविश्वस्तं ब्रह्मण्यं सत्यवादिनम् ॥

meaning.en: He came to the hero who was lying trustingly on a costly bed spread with rich coverings, devoted to brahmins and truthful.

verses.text:
स्वप्नान्ते निशि राजेन्द्र दर्शयामास रश्मिवान् ।
कृपया परयाविष्टः पुत्रस्नेहाच्च भारत ॥

meaning.en: At the end of a dream in the night, king of kings, the radiant one showed himself, filled with great compassion and love for his son.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणो वेदविद्भूत्वा सूर्यो योगाद्धि रूपवान् ।
हितार्थमब्रवीत्कर्णं सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः ॥

meaning.en: Surya, becoming by yoga a handsome brahmin learned in the Vedas, spoke these soothing words to Karna for his good.

verses.text:
कर्ण मद्वचनं तात शृणु सत्यभृतां वर ।
ब्रुवतोऽद्य महाबाहो सौहृदात्परमं हितम् ॥

meaning.en: Karna, dear son, best of those who keep truth, listen to my words; out of friendship I tell you, mighty-armed one, what is for your highest good.

verses.text:
उपायास्यति शक्रस्त्वां पाण्डवानां हितेप्सया ।
ब्राह्मणच्छद्मना कर्ण कुण्डलापजिहीर्षया ॥

meaning.en: Indra will come to you wishing the Pandavas well, Karna, in the disguise of a brahmin, wanting to take your earrings.

verses.text:
विदितं तेन शीलं ते सर्वस्य जगतस्तथा ।
यथा त्वं भिक्षितः सद्भिर्ददास्येव न याचसे ॥

meaning.en: He knows your nature, and the whole world knows it too: when begged by the good you simply give, you do not ask.

verses.text:
त्वं हि तात ददास्येव ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयाचितः ।
वित्तं यच्चान्यदप्याहुर्न प्रत्याख्यासि कर्हिचित् ॥

meaning.en: Dear son, when begged by brahmins you give; whatever wealth or other thing they ask, you never refuse.

verses.text:
तं त्वामेवंविधं ज्ञात्वा स्वयं वै पाकशासनः ।
आगन्ता कुण्डलार्थाय कवचं चैव भिक्षितुम् ॥

meaning.en: Knowing you to be such, Indra himself will come to beg the earrings and the armor.

verses.text:
तस्मै प्रयाचमानाय न देये कुण्डले त्वया ।
अनुनेयः परं शक्त्या श्रेय एतद्धि ते परम् ॥

meaning.en: When he begs, you must not give the earrings; with all your strength you should deflect him, for that is best for you.

verses.text:
कुण्डलार्थे ब्रुवंस्तात कारणैर्बहुभिस्त्वया ।
अन्यैर्बहुविधैर्वित्तैः स निवार्यः पुनः पुनः ॥

meaning.en: When he asks for the earrings, dear son, you should keep turning him back again and again with many reasons and with many other kinds of wealth.

verses.text:
रत्नैः स्त्रीभिस्तथा भोगैर्धनैर्बहुविधैरपि ।
निदर्शनैश्च बहुभिः कुण्डलेप्सुः पुरंदरः ॥

meaning.en: Indra, who wants the earrings, must be put off with jewels, women, pleasures, many kinds of riches, and many examples.

verses.text:
यदि दास्यसि कर्ण त्वं सहजे कुण्डले शुभे ।
आयुषः प्रक्षयं गत्वा मृत्योर्वशमुपेष्यसि ॥

meaning.en: If you give the good, innate earrings, Karna, you will lose your life and fall under the power of death.

verses.text:
कवचेन च संयुक्तः कुण्डलाभ्यां च मानद ।
अवध्यस्त्वं रणेऽरीणामिति विद्धि वचो मम ॥

meaning.en: Equipped with armor and the two earrings, giver of honor, you cannot be killed by enemies in battle; know this as my word.

verses.text:
अमृतादुत्थितं ह्येतदुभयं रत्नसंभवम् ।
तस्माद्रक्ष्यं त्वया कर्ण जीवितं चेत्प्रियं तव ॥

meaning.en: Both of them arose from the nectar and are born of jewels; therefore, Karna, you must guard them if life is dear to you.

verses.text: कर्ण उवाच

meaning.en: Karna said:

verses.text:
को मामेवं भवान्प्राह दर्शयन्सौहृदं परम् ।
कामया भगवन्ब्रूहि को भवान्द्विजवेषधृक् ॥

meaning.en: Who are you, showing me such supreme friendship? Tell me, lord, willingly: who are you in the guise of a brahmin?

verses.text: ब्राह्मण उवाच

meaning.en: The brahmin said:

verses.text:
अहं तात सहस्रांशुः सौहृदात्त्वां निदर्शये ।
कुरुष्वैतद्वचो मे त्वमेतच्छ्रेयः परं हि ते ॥

meaning.en: I am Surya, the thousand-rayed, dear son; out of friendship I show you this. Do as I say, for this is truly your highest good.

verses.text: कर्ण उवाच

meaning.en: Karna said:

verses.text:
श्रेय एव ममात्यन्तं यस्य मे गोपतिः प्रभुः ।
प्रवक्ताद्य हितान्वेषी शृणु चेदं वचो मम ॥

meaning.en: It is surely my highest good that the lord of light himself is today my counselor, seeking my welfare. Listen to my words too.

verses.text:
प्रसादये त्वां वरदं प्रणयाच्च ब्रवीम्यहम् ।
न निवार्यो व्रतादस्मादहं यद्यस्मि ते प्रियः ॥

meaning.en: I appease you, giver of boons, and I speak out of affection: if I am dear to you, do not turn me from this vow.

verses.text:
व्रतं वै मम लोकोऽयं वेत्ति कृत्स्नो विभावसो ।
यथाहं द्विजमुख्येभ्यो दद्यां प्राणानपि ध्रुवम् ॥

meaning.en: The whole world knows my vow, maker of light: that I would surely give even my life to the best of brahmins.

verses.text:
यद्यागच्छति शक्रो मां ब्राह्मणच्छद्मनावृतः ।
हितार्थं पाण्डुपुत्राणां खेचरोत्तम भिक्षितुम् ॥

meaning.en: If Indra comes to me veiled as a brahmin, best of sky-goers, to beg for the good of the sons of Pandu,

verses.text:
दास्यामि विबुधश्रेष्ठ कुण्डले वर्म चोत्तमम् ।
न मे कीर्तिः प्रणश्येत त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता ॥

meaning.en: I will give him, best of gods, the earrings and the excellent armor. Let my fame, renowned in the three worlds, not be destroyed.

verses.text:
मद्विधस्यायशस्यं हि न युक्तं प्राणरक्षणम् ।
युक्तं हि यशसा युक्तं मरणं लोकसंमतम् ॥

meaning.en: For one like me, protecting life at the cost of reputation is not right; death with fame, approved by the world, is right.

verses.text:
सोऽहमिन्द्राय दास्यामि कुण्डले सह वर्मणा ।
यदि मां बलवृत्रघ्नो भिक्षार्थमुपयास्यति ॥

meaning.en: So I shall give Indra the earrings along with the armor, if the slayer of Bala and Vritra comes begging.

verses.text:
हितार्थं पाण्डुपुत्राणां कुण्डले मे प्रयाचितुम् ।
तन्मे कीर्तिकरं लोके तस्याकीर्तिर्भविष्यति ॥

meaning.en: If he asks for my earrings for the good of the Pandavas, that will bring me fame in the world and bring him disrepute.

verses.text:
वृणोमि कीर्तिं लोके हि जीवितेनापि भानुमन् ।
कीर्तिमानश्नुते स्वर्गं हीनकीर्तिस्तु नश्यति ॥

meaning.en: I choose fame in the world even over life, lord of light; the famous win heaven, while one without fame perishes.

verses.text:
कीर्तिर्हि पुरुषं लोके संजीवयति मातृवत् ।
अकीर्तिर्जीवितं हन्ति जीवतोऽपि शरीरिणः ॥

meaning.en: In this world, fame keeps a man alive like a mother; infamy destroys the life of a living person.

verses.text:
अयं पुराणः श्लोको हि स्वयं गीतो विभावसो ।
धात्रा लोकेश्वर यथा कीर्तिरायुर्नरस्य वै ॥

meaning.en: This is an ancient verse sung by the Creator himself, lord of light: fame is a man's life, lord of the world.

verses.text:
पुरुषस्य परे लोके कीर्तिरेव परायणम् ।
इह लोके विशुद्धा च कीर्तिरायुर्विवर्धनी ॥

meaning.en: For a man, fame alone is the refuge in the next world; and pure fame in this world increases life.

verses.text:
सोऽहं शरीरजे दत्त्वा कीर्तिं प्राप्स्यामि शाश्वतीम् ।
दत्त्वा च विधिवद्दानं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यथाविधि ॥

meaning.en: So, by giving what is born with my body, I shall gain eternal fame, and by properly giving gifts to brahmins as prescribed.

verses.text:
हुत्वा शरीरं संग्रामे कृत्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम् ।
विजित्य वा परानाजौ यशः प्राप्स्यामि केवलम् ॥

meaning.en: By offering my body in battle, performing a very difficult deed, or by conquering my enemies in combat, I shall gain glory alone.

verses.text:
भीतानामभयं दत्त्वा संग्रामे जीवितार्थिनाम् ।
वृद्धान्बालान्द्विजातींश्च मोक्षयित्वा महाभयात् ॥

meaning.en: By giving fearless protection to the frightened who seek life in battle, and freeing the aged, children and brahmins from great fear,

verses.text:
प्राप्स्यामि परमं लोके यशः स्वर्भानुसूदन ।
जीवितेनापि मे रक्ष्या कीर्तिस्तद्विद्धि मे व्रतम् ॥

meaning.en: I shall gain the highest glory in the world, slayer of Rahu. Fame must be guarded even at the cost of life; know that as my vow.

verses.text:
सोऽहं दत्त्वा मघवते भिक्षामेतामनुत्तमाम् ।
ब्राह्मणच्छद्मिने देव लोके गन्ता परां गतिम् ॥

meaning.en: So, having given this unequaled alms to Indra, who comes disguised as a brahmin, I shall go to the highest state in the world.
